# The Internship — Subject & Objectives

## Subject {.center}

- Subject stated at the outset — and unchanged through completion: study **lightweight, interpretable text classification**, applied to INSEE's automatic **NAF coding** of business-creation declarations
- Four objectives:

<div class="stage-row">
<div class="stage">
<div class="stage-num">1</div>
<div class="stage-title">Benchmark</div>
<ul><li>Lightweight architectures, benchmarked across datasets of increasing difficulty</li></ul>
</div>
<div class="stage">
<div class="stage-num">2</div>
<div class="stage-title">Understand</div>
<ul><li>Impact of embedding size, vocabulary, layers, attention heads, data volume</li></ul>
</div>
<div class="stage">
<div class="stage-num">3</div>
<div class="stage-title">Explain</div>
<ul><li>Can predictions be trusted enough to support a human decision on ambiguous cases?</li></ul>
</div>
<div class="stage">
<div class="stage-num">4</div>
<div class="stage-title">Exploit hierarchy</div>
<ul><li>NAF is a 5-level nomenclature — can predicting several levels jointly help?</li></ul>
</div>
</div>


## The NAF Nomenclature — A Five-Level Hierarchy {.center}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="42%"}
<p style="font-size:0.52em;color:var(--ink-soft,#4a5578);margin-bottom:0.3em;">Worked example — declared activity: <em>"Clothing retail in a physical store"</em></p>
<div class="hier-diagram">
<div class="hier-level" style="border-left-color:#0f0db0;">
<div class="hier-level-top"><span class="hier-level-name">Section<span class="hier-level-code">letter <b style="color:#0f0db0;">A–U</b></span></span><span class="hier-level-count" style="color:#0f0db0;">20</span></div>
<div class="hier-level-example"><b style="color:#0f0db0;">G</b>Wholesale &amp; retail trade</div>
</div>
<div class="hier-branch"><span class="hier-arrow">↓</span></div>
<div class="hier-level" style="border-left-color:#3f6fd6;">
<div class="hier-level-top"><span class="hier-level-name">Division<span class="hier-level-code"><b style="color:#3f6fd6;">XX</b> · 2 digits</span></span><span class="hier-level-count" style="color:#3f6fd6;">84</span></div>
<div class="hier-level-example"><b style="color:#3f6fd6;">47</b>Retail trade</div>
</div>
<div class="hier-branch"><span class="hier-arrow">↓</span></div>
<div class="hier-level" style="border-left-color:#248bff;">
<div class="hier-level-top"><span class="hier-level-name">Group<span class="hier-level-code">XX.<b style="color:#248bff;">X</b></span></span><span class="hier-level-count" style="color:#248bff;">274</span></div>
<div class="hier-level-example"><b style="color:#248bff;">47.7</b>Other retail sale</div>
</div>
<div class="hier-branch"><span class="hier-arrow">↓</span></div>
<div class="hier-level" style="border-left-color:#7a57ff;">
<div class="hier-level-top"><span class="hier-level-name">Class<span class="hier-level-code">XX.X<b style="color:#7a57ff;">X</b></span></span><span class="hier-level-count" style="color:#7a57ff;">586</span></div>
<div class="hier-level-example"><b style="color:#7a57ff;">47.71</b>Retail sale of clothing</div>
</div>
<div class="hier-branch"><span class="hier-arrow">↓</span></div>
<div class="hier-level" style="border-left-color:#c869ff;">
<div class="hier-level-top"><span class="hier-level-name">Sub-class<span class="hier-level-code">XX.XX<b style="color:#c869ff;">Y</b></span></span><span class="hier-level-count" style="color:#c869ff;">679</span></div>
<div class="hier-level-example"><b style="color:#c869ff;">47.71Z</b>Retail sale of clothing in specialised stores</div>
</div>
</div>
<p style="font-size:0.5em;color:var(--ink-soft,#4a5578);margin-top:0.5em;">The section letter isn't written into the numeric code — it's derived from it (each division belongs to exactly one section).</p>
:::

::: {.column width="58%" .vcenter}
- A company's activity, declared as **free text**, must be assigned a **NAF** code (aligned with **NACE Rev. 2.1**)
- One free-text declaration → one **sub-class**, the finest of the five levels — a 679-way classification problem
:::
::::

# Technical Context

## The Existing System {.center}

- INSEE already runs a **production single-level FastText classifier**, predicting the finest sub-class directly from the free-text declaration
- Raw accuracy isn't the gap. Two things are missing from it:
  - **Explainability** — no way to know *why* the model chose a given label
  - **Smarter mistakes** — when it does get the sub-class wrong, nothing guarantees it at least got the right **section**

## Existing Tools & Technical Environment {.center}

<div style="text-align:center;margin-bottom:0.4em;">
<span class="tag">Python 3.13</span><span class="tag">uv</span><span class="tag">PyTorch</span><span class="tag">PyTorch Lightning</span><span class="tag">Captum</span><span class="tag">Kubernetes / Argo Workflows</span><span class="tag">Quarto</span><span class="tag">SSP Cloud (Onyxia)</span><span class="tag">S3 / MinIO</span>
</div>

- **`torchTextClassifiers`** — INSEE's own open-source PyTorch/Lightning package, a unified interface across every architecture compared
- All experiments run on **SSP Cloud "Onyxia"**, INSEE's Kubernetes-based datalab

# Contributions & Results

## Methodology: A Progressive Testbed {.center}

Rather than start directly on NAF's ~700 classes, the whole pipeline — training, prediction analysis, explainability — was built and validated on two public benchmarks first, in increasing order of difficulty.

<div class="stage-row">
<div class="stage">
<div class="stage-num">1</div>
<div class="stage-title">Amazon Reviews</div>
<ul><li>5-class sentiment (1–5★)</li><li>~200,000 reviews</li></ul>
</div>
<div class="stage-arrow">→</div>
<div class="stage">
<div class="stage-num">2</div>
<div class="stage-title">CLINC150</div>
<ul><li>150-class intent detection</li><li>~15,000 utterances</li></ul>
</div>
<div class="stage-arrow">→</div>
<div class="stage">
<div class="stage-num">3</div>
<div class="stage-title">NAF</div>
<ul><li>Target application</li><li>~1.2M+ declarations</li></ul>
</div>
</div>

### FATE (Transformer)

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="34%"}
- Same embeddings, but first passed through **N transformer encoder layers** (self-attention + feed-forward)
- Words gain **context from their neighbors** before being pooled
- More expressive representation — but heavier and slower to train/run
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}

## Aggregation Methods {.center}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Mean Pooling

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="34%"}
- Every token embedding contributes **equally** to the sentence vector: v = (1/T) · Σ<sub>t</sub> e<sub>t</sub>
- The **same pooled vector** *v* is then reused by the linear head, for every class alike
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}

### Label Attention

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="34%"}
- Each class *c* learns its own **attention query**, giving weights α<sub>c,t</sub> over the tokens (softmax, sums to 1)
- Class vector: v<sub>c</sub> = Σ<sub>t</sub> α<sub>c,t</sub> · e<sub>t</sub> — a **different weighted combination per class**
- The weights double as an **explanation**: which words mattered, *for which class*
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}

## Amazon: Hyperparameter Sweep {.smaller}

960 runs on Amazon, swept across architecture and embedding dimension.

```{python}
#| label: load-amazon-runs-train

from pathlib import Path
import mlflow
import pandas as pd

REMOTE_BASE = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/runs_csvs"
CACHE_PATH = Path("runs_csvs/amazon/runs.csv")
CACHE_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

def arch_label(row):
    la = str(row["n_heads_label_attn"]) == "4"
    if row["n_layers"] == 0:
        return "FastText + Label Attention" if la else "FastText"
    suffix = " + Label Attention" if la else ""
    return f"FATE (L={row['n_layers']}){suffix}"

if CACHE_PATH.exists():
    df = pd.read_csv(CACHE_PATH)
    if "metrics.train_time_s" in df.columns:
        df = df.rename(columns={"metrics.train_time_s": "train_time_s"})
else:
    try:
        df = pd.read_csv(f"{REMOTE_BASE}/amazon/runs.csv")
    except Exception:
        df = mlflow.search_runs(experiment_names=["amazon"], max_results=2000)
        df = df[df["status"] == "FINISHED"].copy()
        df = df.rename(columns={
            "params.emb_dim":                  "emb_dim",
            "params.n_layers":                 "n_layers",
            "params.n_head":                   "n_head",
            "params.n_heads_label_attention":  "n_heads_label_attn",
            "params.vocab_size":               "vocab_size",
            "params.lr":                       "lr",
            "metrics.num_params":              "num_params",
            "metrics.test_accuracy":           "test_accuracy",
            "metrics.test_f1_macro":           "test_f1_macro",
            "metrics.train_time_s":            "train_time_s",
        })

        client = mlflow.MlflowClient()
        def get_min_val_loss(run_id):
            history = client.get_metric_history(run_id, "val_loss")
            return min(m.value for m in history) if history else None

        df["min_val_loss"] = df["run_id"].apply(get_min_val_loss)

        for col in ["emb_dim", "n_layers", "vocab_size"]:
            df[col] = df[col].astype(int)
        df["lr"] = df["lr"].astype(float)
        df["num_params"] = df["num_params"].astype(int)
        df["architecture"] = df.apply(arch_label, axis=1)

    df.to_csv(CACHE_PATH, index=False)

COLORS = {
    "FastText":                          "#2196F3",
    "FastText + Label Attention":        "#00BCD4",
    "FATE (L=1)":                        "#FFC107",
    "FATE (L=1) + Label Attention":      "#FF8C00",
    "FATE (L=2)":                        "#CC0000",
    "FATE (L=2) + Label Attention":      "#880E4F",
    "FATE (L=4)":                        "#6A1B9A",
    "FATE (L=4) + Label Attention":      "#311B92",
}
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### vs. Parameters

```{python}
#| label: fig-pareto-slide
#| fig-cap: "Validation loss vs. number of parameters"

import plotly.graph_objects as go

df_curves = (
    df.groupby(["architecture", "emb_dim", "vocab_size", "num_params"], as_index=False)
    ["min_val_loss"].min()
    .sort_values("num_params")
)

ft_archs   = ["FastText", "FastText + Label Attention"]
df_ft      = df[df["architecture"].isin(ft_archs)].groupby(
    ["architecture", "emb_dim", "vocab_size", "lr", "num_params"], as_index=False
)["min_val_loss"].min()
df_scatter = pd.concat([df_ft, df[~df["architecture"].isin(ft_archs)]], ignore_index=True)

fig = go.Figure()

for arch in COLORS:
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[None], y=[None], mode="markers",
        name=arch, legendgroup=arch, showlegend=True,
        marker=dict(color=COLORS[arch], size=8, opacity=1.0),
    ))

for arch, group in df_scatter.groupby("architecture"):
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=group["num_params"], y=group["min_val_loss"],
        mode="markers", name=arch, legendgroup=arch, showlegend=False,
        marker=dict(color=COLORS.get(arch, "grey"), size=5, opacity=0.3),
        hovertemplate="params=%{x:,}<br>val_loss=%{y:.4f}<extra>" + arch + "</extra>",
    ))

for arch, group in df_curves.groupby("architecture"):
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=group["num_params"], y=group["min_val_loss"],
        mode="lines+markers", name=arch, legendgroup=arch, showlegend=False,
        line=dict(color=COLORS.get(arch, "grey"), width=2), marker=dict(size=5),
        hovertemplate="params=%{x:,}<br>best val_loss=%{y:.4f}<extra>" + arch + "</extra>",
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Number of parameters", yaxis_title="Validation loss",
    legend_title="Architecture", height=460,
    xaxis=dict(tickformat=".2s"), margin=dict(l=50, r=10, t=10, b=40),
)
fig.show()
```

```{python}
    height=460, width=860, margin=dict(l=50, r=10, t=10, b=40),
)
fig.show()
```

## Amazon: Predictions {.smaller}

```{python}
#| label: load-predictions-slide

import numpy as np, urllib.request
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots

STAR_LABELS  = ["1★", "2★", "3★", "4★", "5★"]

PRED_BUCKET  = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/predictions/amazon"
ARCH_FILES   = {
    "FastText":                          "fasttext.npz",
    "FastText + Label Attention":        "fasttext_labatt.npz",
    "FATE (L=1)":                        "fateL1.npz",
    "FATE (L=1) + Label Attention":      "fateL1_labatt.npz",
    "FATE (L=2)":                        "fateL2.npz",
    "FATE (L=2) + Label Attention":      "fateL2_labatt.npz",
    "FATE (L=4)":                        "fateL4.npz",
    "FATE (L=4) + Label Attention":      "fateL4_labatt.npz",
}

PREDS_DIR = Path("results/amazon/preds")
PREDS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

preds_by_arch = {}
for arch, fname in ARCH_FILES.items():
    cache = PREDS_DIR / fname
    try:
        if not cache.exists():
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{PRED_BUCKET}/{fname}", cache)
        d = np.load(cache, allow_pickle=True)
        preds_by_arch[arch] = {
            "y_test": d["y_test"].astype(int),
            "y_pred": d["y_pred"].astype(int),
        }
    except Exception:
        pass

ARCHS_AVAIL = list(preds_by_arch.keys())
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Error Analysis

```{python}
#| label: fig-error-seg-slide
#| fig-cap: "Prediction distance per architecture"

SEG_KEYS   = ["Correct", "Off by 1", "Off by 2", "Off by 3+"]
SEG_COLORS = {"Correct": "#43A047", "Off by 1": "#FDD835", "Off by 2": "#FB8C00", "Off by 3+": "#E53935"}

arch_segs = {}
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL:
    d        = preds_by_arch[arch]
    y_t, y_p = d["y_test"], d["y_pred"]
    dist     = np.abs(y_p - y_t)
    n        = len(dist)
    arch_segs[arch] = {
        "Correct":   (dist == 0).sum() / n * 100,
        "Off by 1":  (dist == 1).sum() / n * 100,
        "Off by 2":  (dist == 2).sum() / n * 100,
        "Off by 3+": (dist >= 3).sum() / n * 100,
    }

fig1 = go.Figure()
for i, arch in enumerate(ARCHS_AVAIL):
    segs = arch_segs[arch]
    for seg in SEG_KEYS:
        pct = segs[seg]
        fig1.add_trace(go.Bar(
            x=[pct], y=[arch], orientation="h",
            name=seg, legendgroup=seg, showlegend=(i == 0),
            marker_color=SEG_COLORS[seg],
            text=f"{pct:.1f}%" if pct >= 4 else "",
            textposition="inside", insidetextanchor="middle",
            textfont=dict(size=11, color="white" if seg != "Off by 1" else "#333"),
            hovertemplate=f"<b>{seg}</b>: {pct:.1f}%<extra></extra>",
        ))

fig1.update_layout(
    barmode="relative",
    template="simple_white",
    xaxis=dict(range=[0, 100], ticksuffix="%", showgrid=False, title_text="% of test examples"),
    yaxis=dict(autorange="reversed"),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", x=0.5, xanchor="center", y=-0.22, yanchor="top",
                itemclick=False, itemdoubleclick=False),
    height=380, width=820, margin=dict(t=20, b=80),
)
fig1.show()
```

- The vast majority of predictions land within **±1 star** of the truth — off-by-3+ errors stay under **8%**

```{python}
from IPython.display import HTML, display

EXPLAIN_BUCKET = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/explanations/amazon"

_ARTIFACT_NAMES = ["captum.npz", "label_attn.npz", "class_vectors.npz", "self_attn.npz", "faithfulness.npz"]
_NOT_APPLICABLE = {("pooling", "label_attn.npz")}  # mean pooling has no label attention mechanism

def _load_artifact(method: str, name: str):
    """Fetch (and cache) one explainability artifact; None if unavailable."""
    if (method, name) in _NOT_APPLICABLE:
        return None
    cache_dir = Path("results/amazon/explain") / method
    cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cache = cache_dir / name
    try:
        if not cache.exists():
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{EXPLAIN_BUCKET}/{method}/{name}", cache)
        return np.load(cache, allow_pickle=True)
    except Exception:
        return None

cap_la, lat_la, cv_la, sa_la, fai_la = (_load_artifact("labatt",  n) for n in _ARTIFACT_NAMES)
cap_pl, lat_pl, cv_pl, sa_pl, fai_pl = (_load_artifact("pooling", n) for n in _ARTIFACT_NAMES)
fai_la_lw = _load_artifact("labatt", "faithfulness_labatt_weight.npz")  # labatt only: guided by its own attention weights instead of Captum

HAS_LA   = cap_la is not None
HAS_PL   = cap_pl is not None
HAS_BOTH = HAS_LA and HAS_PL

if not HAS_LA:
    print("Explainability artifacts not yet available — re-run src/explain.py")
else:
    N_CLS   = cap_la["word_attn"][0].shape[0]
    STARS   = [f"{i + 1}★" for i in range(N_CLS)]
    PALETTE = ["#1565C0", "#2E7D32", "#F57F17", "#6A1B9A", "#B71C1C"]

    MODEL_LABELS = {"labatt": "Label Attention", "pooling": "Mean Pooling"}
    CAPTUM       = {"labatt": cap_la, "pooling": cap_pl}
    LABEL_ATTN   = {"labatt": lat_la, "pooling": lat_pl}
    CLASS_VECS   = {"labatt": cv_la,  "pooling": cv_pl}
    SELF_ATTN    = {"labatt": sa_la,  "pooling": sa_pl}
    FAITHFUL     = {"labatt": fai_la, "pooling": fai_pl}
    FAITHFUL_LW  = fai_la_lw
    MODEL_KEYS   = [k for k in ("labatt", "pooling") if CAPTUM[k] is not None]

    def _class_sorted(cap, i: int) -> np.ndarray:
        """Reorder word_attn[i]'s rows from confidence rank back to actual class index."""
        inv = np.argsort(cap["class_order"][i])
        return cap["word_attn"][i][inv]
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Word Attributions

Each word's background is shaded by its attribution score for the selected class — **green = pushes toward it, red = pushes away**. For Label Attention's own weights (third row), **blue intensity = share of attention received** — unsigned, since attention weights can't push away from a class, only toward it.

```{python}
        rng.shuffle(agree_ok)

        both_wrong = np.where((y_pred_la != y_true_la) & (y_pred_pl != y_true_la))[0]
        rng.shuffle(both_wrong)
        picks += [int(i) for i in both_wrong if i not in picks][:2]
        pl_right_la_wrong = np.where((y_pred_pl == y_true_la) & (y_pred_la != y_true_la))[0]
        rng.shuffle(pl_right_la_wrong)

    else:

    return words.map(function(w, j) {{
      const s     = j < scores.length ? scores[j] : 0;
      const t     = Math.abs(s) / amax;
      const rgb   = s >= 0 ? '57,255,20' : '255,30,30';

      return '<span style="background-color:rgba(' + rgb + ',' + alpha + ');'

           + esc(w) + '</span>';
    }}).join(' ');

  function spansUnsigned(words, scores) {{
    const amax = Math.max.apply(null, scores.map(function(x){{ return Math.abs(x); }})) || 1;
    return words.map(function(w, j) {{
      const s     = j < scores.length ? scores[j] : 0;
      const t     = Math.abs(s) / amax;
      const alpha = (0.10 + 0.65 * t).toFixed(2);
      return '<span style="background-color:rgba(21,101,192,' + alpha + ');'
           + 'padding:1px 3px;margin:0 1px;line-height:2.3;">'
           + esc(w) + '</span>';

    let h = '';

      const ok   = m.pred === e.y_true;
      const bc   = ok ? '#2E7D32' : '#B71C1C';
      const skey = i + '_' + k;

      const btns = ST.map(function(star, c) {{

        return '<button class="hl-cls-btn" onclick="hlSelClass(' + i + ',' + k + ',' + c + ')"'
             + ' style="border-color:' + col + ';color:' + (active ? '#fff' : col) + ';background:' + (active ? col : '#fff') + ';">'

        +  '<span style="color:#222;font-weight:700;">' + ST[m.pred] + '</span> '
        +  '<span style="color:' + bc + ';font-size:11px;">(' + (ok ? '✓ correct' : '✗ incorrect') + ')</span>'
        +  ' &nbsp;&middot;&nbsp; <span style="font-size:11px;color:#888;">attributions for:</span> ' + btns
        +  '</div>'
        +  '<div class="hl-words">' + (m.kind === 'unsigned' ? spansUnsigned(m.words, m.class_scores[selC]) : spansSigned(m.words, m.class_scores[selC])) + '</div>'
        +  '</div>';
    }}
    document.getElementById('hl-models').innerHTML = h;
  }}

  window.hlSelClass = function(exIdx, modelIdx, classIdx) {{
    hlSel[exIdx + '_' + modelIdx] = classIdx;
    render(cur);
  }};
  window.hlNav = function(d) {{ cur = (cur + d + EX.length) % EX.length; render(cur); }};
  render(0);
}})();
</script>
```

## CLINC150: Hyperparameter Sweep {.smaller}

```{python}
#| label: fetch-mlflow-clinc150

import mlflow, os

RENAME_COLS = {
    "params.emb_dim":                  "emb_dim",
    "params.n_layers":                 "n_layers",
    "params.n_head":                   "n_head",
    "params.n_heads_label_attention":  "n_heads_label_attn",
    "params.vocab_size":               "vocab_size",
    "params.lr":                       "lr",
    "metrics.num_params":              "num_params",
    "metrics.test_accuracy":           "test_accuracy",
    "metrics.test_f1_macro":           "test_f1_macro",
    "metrics.train_time_s":            "train_time_s",
    "metrics.val_loss":                "min_val_loss",
}
KEY_COLS = ["n_layers", "emb_dim", "vocab_size", "n_head", "n_heads_label_attn", "lr"]

def fetch_runs_clinc(experiment_name: str, cache_path: Path) -> pd.DataFrame:
    cache_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if cache_path.exists():
        return pd.read_csv(cache_path)
    try:
        raw = pd.read_csv(f"{REMOTE_BASE}/{cache_path.relative_to('runs_csvs')}")
    except Exception:
        raw = mlflow.search_runs(experiment_names=[experiment_name], max_results=5000)
        raw = raw[raw["status"] == "FINISHED"].copy()
        raw = raw.rename(columns={k: v for k, v in RENAME_COLS.items() if k in raw.columns})
        for col in ["emb_dim", "n_layers", "vocab_size"]:
            raw[col] = pd.to_numeric(raw[col], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
        raw["lr"]         = raw["lr"].astype(float)
        raw["num_params"] = pd.to_numeric(raw["num_params"], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
        raw["architecture"] = raw.apply(arch_label, axis=1)
        raw = raw.sort_values("min_val_loss").drop_duplicates(subset=KEY_COLS, keep="first")
    raw.to_csv(cache_path, index=False)
    return raw

# clinc150 without the out-of-scope class — the version used throughout the report
df_clinc = fetch_runs_clinc("clinc150_noos", Path("runs_csvs/clinc150/runs_no_oos.csv"))

# The target vocab_size=10,000 saturated at the dataset's actual vocabulary,
# producing three near-identical values (8,406 / 8,407 / 8,408) across seeds.
# Collapse them to their average so they form a single dimension.
df_clinc["vocab_size"] = df_clinc["vocab_size"].replace({8406: 8407, 8408: 8407})
```

```{python}

}

df_curves_clinc = (
    df_clinc.groupby(["architecture", "emb_dim", "vocab_size", "num_params"], as_index=False)
    ["min_val_loss"].min()
    .sort_values("num_params")
)

ft_archs_clinc = ["FastText", "FastText + Label Attention"]
df_ft_clinc    = df_clinc[df_clinc["architecture"].isin(ft_archs_clinc)].groupby(
    ["architecture", "emb_dim", "vocab_size", "lr", "num_params"], as_index=False
)["min_val_loss"].min()
df_scatter_clinc = pd.concat(
    [df_ft_clinc, df_clinc[~df_clinc["architecture"].isin(ft_archs_clinc)]], ignore_index=True
)

fig = go.Figure()

for arch in COLORS_CLINC:
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=[None], y=[None], mode="markers",
        name=arch, legendgroup=arch, showlegend=True,
        marker=dict(color=COLORS_CLINC[arch], size=8, opacity=1.0),
    ))

for arch, group in df_scatter_clinc.groupby("architecture"):
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=group["num_params"], y=group["min_val_loss"],
        mode="markers", name=arch, legendgroup=arch, showlegend=False,
        marker=dict(color=COLORS_CLINC.get(arch, "grey"), size=5, opacity=0.3),
        hovertemplate="params=%{x:,}<br>val_loss=%{y:.4f}<extra>" + arch + "</extra>",
    ))

for arch, group in df_curves_clinc.groupby("architecture"):
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=group["num_params"], y=group["min_val_loss"],
        mode="lines+markers", name=arch, legendgroup=arch, showlegend=False,
        line=dict(color=COLORS_CLINC.get(arch, "grey"), width=2), marker=dict(size=5),
        hovertemplate="params=%{x:,}<br>best val_loss=%{y:.4f}<extra>" + arch + "</extra>",
    ))

y_cap_clinc = df_clinc["min_val_loss"].quantile(0.92)
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Number of parameters",
    yaxis_title="Validation loss",
    legend_title="Architecture",
    height=460,
    xaxis=dict(tickformat=".2s"),
    yaxis=dict(range=[df_clinc["min_val_loss"].min() * 0.98, y_cap_clinc]),
    margin=dict(l=50, r=10, t=10, b=40),
)
fig.show()
```

A clear gap: **label attention consistently hurts** here, unlike on Amazon. Suspected cause — not enough data per class: 150 classes for 15,000 examples here, vs. 5 classes for 200k on Amazon, so building a good class representation is much harder. We'll confirm this later.

## CLINC150: Explainability {.smaller}

```{python}
#| label: load-explain-artifacts-clinc

EXPLAIN_BUCKET_CLINC = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/explanations/clinc150"

def _load_artifact_clinc(method: str, name: str):
    if (method, name) in _NOT_APPLICABLE:
        return None
    cache_dir = Path("results/clinc150/explain") / method
    cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cache = cache_dir / name
    try:
        if not cache.exists():
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{EXPLAIN_BUCKET_CLINC}/{method}/{name}", cache)
        return np.load(cache, allow_pickle=True)
    except Exception:
        return None

cap_la_c, lat_la_c, cv_la_c, sa_la_c, fai_la_c = (_load_artifact_clinc("labatt",  n) for n in _ARTIFACT_NAMES)
cap_pl_c, lat_pl_c, cv_pl_c, sa_pl_c, fai_pl_c = (_load_artifact_clinc("pooling", n) for n in _ARTIFACT_NAMES)

HAS_LA_C = cap_la_c is not None

if not HAS_LA_C:
    print("Explainability artifacts not yet available — re-run src/explain.py")
else:
    N_CLS_C = cap_la_c["word_attn"][0].shape[0]

    if "class_names" in cap_la_c.files:
        CLASS_NAMES = [str(c) for c in cap_la_c["class_names"]]
    else:
        with open("assets/clinc150_labels.json") as _f:
            _lmap = json.load(_f)
        CLASS_NAMES = [_lmap[str(i)] for i in range(N_CLS_C)]
```

```{python}
#| label: selfattn-setup-clinc

HAS_PL_C   = cap_pl_c is not None
HAS_BOTH_C = HAS_LA_C and HAS_PL_C

MODEL_LABELS = {"labatt": "Label Attention", "pooling": "Mean Pooling"}
CAPTUM    = {"labatt": cap_la_c, "pooling": cap_pl_c}
SELF_ATTN = {"labatt": sa_la_c,  "pooling": sa_pl_c}
MODEL_KEYS = [k for k in ("labatt", "pooling") if CAPTUM[k] is not None]

HAS_LA   = HAS_LA_C
HAS_PL   = HAS_PL_C
HAS_BOTH = HAS_BOTH_C
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-explain-selfattn-clinc
#| fig-cap: "Self-attention matrices per head and per layer, for a sampled CLINC150 utterance."

HAS_SA       = HAS_LA and all(SELF_ATTN.get(k) is not None for k in MODEL_KEYS)
HAS_PER_HEAD = HAS_SA and all("self_attn_per_head" in SELF_ATTN[k].files for k in MODEL_KEYS)

if not HAS_PER_HEAD:
    print("Per-head self-attention artifacts not yet available.")
else:
    HAS_TOKENS = "tokens" in SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]].files

    n_align  = min(len(SELF_ATTN[k]["texts"]) for k in MODEL_KEYS)
    lengths  = [SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]]["self_attn"][i].shape[-1] for i in range(n_align)]
    mid_idx  = np.array([i for i, L in enumerate(lengths) if 8 <= L <= 18])

    rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
    cand_idx: list = []

    if len(mid_idx) == 0:
        cand_idx = [int(np.argmax(lengths))]
    elif HAS_BOTH:
        y_true_ref = SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]]["y_true"].astype(int)[mid_idx]
        y_pred_a   = SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]]["y_pred"].astype(int)[mid_idx]
        y_pred_b   = SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[1]]["y_pred"].astype(int)[mid_idx]

        def _pick(mask, k):
            pool = mid_idx[mask].tolist()
            rng.shuffle(pool)
            added = 0
            for i in pool:
                if i in cand_idx:
                    continue
                cand_idx.append(int(i))
                added += 1
                if added >= k:
                    break

        _pick(y_pred_a != y_pred_b, 2)                                # disagree
        _pick((y_pred_a == y_pred_b) & (y_pred_a == y_true_ref), 2)   # both correct
        _pick((y_pred_a != y_true_ref) & (y_pred_b != y_true_ref), 2) # both wrong
        _pick((y_pred_b == y_true_ref) & (y_pred_a != y_true_ref), 1) # MODEL_KEYS[1] right, MODEL_KEYS[0] wrong
        _pick((y_pred_a == y_true_ref) & (y_pred_b != y_true_ref), 1) # MODEL_KEYS[0] right, MODEL_KEYS[1] wrong
        if not cand_idx:
            cand_idx = mid_idx[:8].tolist()
    else:
        cand_idx = mid_idx[:8].tolist()

    n_layers_ph = min(SELF_ATTN[k]["self_attn_per_head"][cand_idx[0]].shape[0] for k in MODEL_KEYS)
    n_heads_ph  = min(SELF_ATTN[k]["self_attn_per_head"][cand_idx[0]].shape[1] for k in MODEL_KEYS)
    n_models    = len(MODEL_KEYS)

    def _tokens_for(key, idx, L):
        if HAS_TOKENS:
            return list(SELF_ATTN[key]["tokens"][idx])[:L]
        raw = str(SELF_ATTN[key]["texts"][idx]).split()
        return (raw + [""] * L)[:L]

    def _title_for(idx):
        text   = str(SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]]["texts"][idx])
        y_true = int(SELF_ATTN[MODEL_KEYS[0]]["y_true"][idx])
        bits   = [f"true: <b>{CLASS_NAMES[y_true]}</b>"]
        for key in MODEL_KEYS:
            y_pred = int(SELF_ATTN[key]["y_pred"][idx])
            ok     = y_pred == y_true
            mark   = "✓" if ok else "✗"
            col    = "#2E7D32" if ok else "#B71C1C"
            bits.append(
                f"{MODEL_LABELS[key]} → "
                f"<span style='color:{col};font-weight:700;'>{CLASS_NAMES[y_pred]} {mark}</span>"
            )
        return f'Per-head self-attention — "{text}"<br>' + " · ".join(bits)

    def _layer_frame(idx, layer):
        per_head = {k: SELF_ATTN[k]["self_attn_per_head"][idx] for k in MODEL_KEYS}
        z_list, x_list, y_list = [], [], []
        for key in MODEL_KEYS:
            mat_layer = per_head[key][layer]
            L_k  = mat_layer.shape[-1]
            tok_k = _tokens_for(key, idx, L_k)
            for h in range(n_heads_ph):
                z_list.append(mat_layer[h])
                x_list.append(tok_k)
                y_list.append(tok_k)
        return z_list, x_list, y_list

    def _frame_for(idx):
        layers = []
        for layer in range(n_layers_ph):
            z_l, x_l, y_l = _layer_frame(idx, layer)
            layers.append({"z": [zz.tolist() for zz in z_l], "x": x_l, "y": y_l})
        return {"title": _title_for(idx), "layers": layers}

    frame0 = _frame_for(cand_idx[0])

    cell_px = 17
    tok_n   = len(frame0["layers"][0]["x"][0])
    plot_sz = tok_n * cell_px

    div_ids = [f"selfattn-fig-slide-l{layer + 1}" for layer in range(n_layers_ph)]
    fig_blocks_html = []
    for layer in range(n_layers_ph):
        fig_l = make_subplots(
            rows=n_models, cols=n_heads_ph,
            column_titles=[f"Head {h + 1}" for h in range(n_heads_ph)],
            row_titles=[f"<b>{MODEL_LABELS[k]}</b>" for k in MODEL_KEYS],
            horizontal_spacing=0.04, vertical_spacing=0.18,
        )
        z_l = frame0["layers"][layer]["z"]
        x_l = frame0["layers"][layer]["x"]
        y_l = frame0["layers"][layer]["y"]
        trace_i = 0
        for ri, key in enumerate(MODEL_KEYS):
            row    = ri + 1
            for h in range(n_heads_ph):
                col    = h + 1
                show_y = (col == 1)
                idx_sp = (row - 1) * n_heads_ph + col
                xref   = "x" if idx_sp == 1 else f"x{idx_sp}"
                fig_l.add_trace(go.Heatmap(
                    z=z_l[trace_i], x=x_l[trace_i], y=y_l[trace_i],
                    coloraxis="coloraxis",
                    hovertemplate="key=%{x}<br>query=%{y}<br>weight=%{z:.3f}"
                                  + f"<extra>{MODEL_LABELS[key]} L{layer + 1} H{h + 1}</extra>",
                ), row=row, col=col)
                trace_i += 1
                fig_l.update_xaxes(
                    tickangle=-90, tickfont=dict(size=9), dtick=1,
                    showticklabels=True, row=row, col=col,
                )
                fig_l.update_yaxes(
                    autorange="reversed", showticklabels=show_y, tickfont=dict(size=9), dtick=1,
                    scaleanchor=xref, scaleratio=1, row=row, col=col,
                )

        for ann in fig_l.layout.annotations:
            ann.font.size = 11

        fig_height = plot_sz * n_models + 155
        fig_l.update_layout(
            width=plot_sz * n_heads_ph + 180,
            height=fig_height,
            paper_bgcolor="white", plot_bgcolor="white",
            margin=dict(t=50, b=75, l=30, r=100),
            coloraxis=dict(colorscale="Viridis", cmin=0, colorbar=dict(title="weight", len=0.8, thickness=14)),
            showlegend=False,
        )

        x0_dom = fig_l.layout.xaxis.domain[0]
        last_xaxis = "xaxis" if n_heads_ph == 1 else f"xaxis{n_heads_ph}"
        x1_dom = fig_l.layout[last_xaxis].domain[1]
        y_bracket_bot = 1 + 20 / fig_height
        y_bracket_top = 1 + 25 / fig_height
        y_label       = 1 + 29 / fig_height
        fig_l.add_shape(
            type="path",
            path=f"M {x0_dom},{y_bracket_bot} L {x0_dom},{y_bracket_top} "
                 f"L {x1_dom},{y_bracket_top} L {x1_dom},{y_bracket_bot}",
            xref="paper", yref="paper", line=dict(color="#999", width=1),
        )
        fig_l.add_annotation(
            xref="paper", yref="paper",
            x=(x0_dom + x1_dom) / 2, y=y_label,
            text=f"<b>Layer {layer + 1}</b>", showarrow=False,
            font=dict(size=12), xanchor="center", yanchor="bottom",
        )

        fig_blocks_html.append(
            fig_l.to_html(full_html=False, include_plotlyjs=False, div_id=div_ids[layer])
        )

    frames = [_frame_for(idx) for idx in cand_idx]

    title_id = "sa-title-slide"
    blocks_html = "".join(
        f'<div style="margin-top:{18 if layer == 0 else 0}px;">{fig_blocks_html[layer]}</div>'
        for layer in range(n_layers_ph)
    )

    nav_html = f"""
<style>
  .sa-nav   {{ display:flex; align-items:center; gap:12px;
               justify-content:center; margin-bottom:8px; }}
  .sa-btn   {{ padding:6px 18px; background:#f0f0f0; border:1px solid #ccc;
               border-radius:5px; cursor:pointer; font-size:13px; }}
  .sa-btn:hover {{ background:#e0e0e0; }}
  .sa-count {{ font-size:12px; color:#999; }}
  .sa-title {{ text-align:center; font-size:13px; line-height:1.5; margin-bottom:6px; }}
  .sa-blocks {{ overflow-x:auto; }}
</style>
<div class="sa-nav">
  <button class="sa-btn" onclick="selfAttnNavSlide(-1)">← Prev</button>
  <span class="sa-count" id="sa-count-slide"></span>
  <button class="sa-btn" onclick="selfAttnNavSlide(1)">Next →</button>
</div>
<div class="sa-title" id="{title_id}">{frame0["title"]}</div>
<div class="sa-blocks">
{blocks_html}
</div>
<script>
(function() {{
  const FRAMES  = {json.dumps(frames)};
  const DIV_IDS = {json.dumps(div_ids)};
  let cur = 0;
  window.selfAttnNavSlide = function(d) {{
    cur = (cur + d + FRAMES.length) % FRAMES.length;

  }};
  document.getElementById("sa-count-slide").textContent = "1 / " + FRAMES.length;

"""
    display(HTML(nav_html))
```

## NAF: The Core of the Project {.center}

Amazon and CLINC150 were the testbed. **NAF is the target application** — automatic coding of business-creation declarations, at production scale.

## Label Attention: The Payoff {.center}

:::: {.columns style="align-items:center;"}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{python}
#| label: fetch-mlflow-naf

RENAME_COLS = {
    "params.emb_dim":                  "emb_dim",
    "params.n_layers":                 "n_layers",
    "params.n_head":                   "n_head",
    "params.n_heads_label_attention":  "n_heads_label_attn",
    "params.vocab_size":               "vocab_size",
    "params.lr":                       "lr",
    "metrics.num_params":              "num_params",
    "metrics.test_accuracy":           "test_accuracy",
    "metrics.test_f1_macro":           "test_f1_macro",
    "metrics.train_time_s":            "train_time_s",
    "metrics.val_loss":                "min_val_loss",
}
KEY_COLS = ["n_layers", "emb_dim", "vocab_size", "n_head", "n_heads_label_attn", "lr"]

def fetch_runs_naf(experiment_name: str, cache_path: Path, train_fraction: float) -> pd.DataFrame:
    cache_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if cache_path.exists():
        return pd.read_csv(cache_path)
    try:
        raw = pd.read_csv(f"{REMOTE_BASE}/{cache_path.relative_to('runs_csvs')}")
    except Exception:
        raw = mlflow.search_runs(experiment_names=[experiment_name], max_results=5000)
        raw = raw[raw["status"] == "FINISHED"].copy()
        raw = raw[pd.to_numeric(raw["params.train_fraction"], errors="coerce") == train_fraction]
        raw = raw.rename(columns={k: v for k, v in RENAME_COLS.items() if k in raw.columns})
        for col in ["emb_dim", "n_layers", "vocab_size"]:
            raw[col] = pd.to_numeric(raw[col], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
        raw["lr"]         = raw["lr"].astype(float)
        raw["num_params"] = pd.to_numeric(raw["num_params"], errors="coerce").astype("Int64")
        raw["architecture"] = raw.apply(arch_label, axis=1)
        raw = raw.sort_values("min_val_loss").drop_duplicates(subset=KEY_COLS, keep="first")
    raw.to_csv(cache_path, index=False)
    return raw

df_frac13  = fetch_runs_naf("naf", Path("runs_csvs/naf/runs_frac13.csv"),  train_fraction=0.13)
df_frac26  = fetch_runs_naf("naf", Path("runs_csvs/naf/runs_frac26.csv"),  train_fraction=0.26)
df_frac52  = fetch_runs_naf("naf", Path("runs_csvs/naf/runs_frac52.csv"),  train_fraction=0.52)
df_frac100 = fetch_runs_naf("naf", Path("runs_csvs/naf/runs_frac100.csv"), train_fraction=1.0)
```

This confirms the hypothesis from CLINC150: label attention needs enough data per class to learn useful queries, and only pays off once that data is available — exactly what happens here, at full NAF scale.

## NAF: Predictions {.smaller}

```{python}
#| label: load-predictions-naf

import json
from collections import defaultdict

PRED_BUCKET = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/predictions/naf"
ARCH_FILES  = {
    "FastText":                   "fasttext.npz",
    "FastText + Label Attention": "fasttext_labatt.npz",
}

PREDS_DIR = Path("results/naf/preds")
PREDS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

preds_by_arch = {}
for arch, fname in ARCH_FILES.items():
    cache = PREDS_DIR / fname
    try:
        if not cache.exists():
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{PRED_BUCKET}/{fname}", cache)
        d = np.load(cache, allow_pickle=True)
        preds_by_arch[arch] = {
            "y_test": d["y_test"].astype(int),
            "y_pred": d["y_pred"].astype(int),
            "X_test": d["X_test"],
        }
    except Exception:
        pass

ARCHS_AVAIL = list(preds_by_arch.keys())

with open("assets/naf_labels.json") as f:
    NAF_LABEL_MAP = json.load(f)

with open("assets/naf2025_structure.json") as f:
    _naf_struct = json.load(f)

DIVISION_TO_SECTION = {
    div: s["id"] for s in _naf_struct["sections"] for div in s["divisions"]
}
SECTION_LABEL = {s["id"]: s["label"] for s in _naf_struct["sections"]}
SOUSCLASSE_LABEL = _naf_struct["sousclasses"]

def class_code(idx: int) -> str:
    return NAF_LABEL_MAP.get(str(idx), "?")

def code_section(code: str) -> str:
    return DIVISION_TO_SECTION.get(code[:2], "?")

def code_division(code: str) -> str:
    return code[:2]

def code_groupe(code: str) -> str:
    return code[:2] + "." + code[2:3]

def code_classe(code: str) -> str:
    return code[:2] + "." + code[2:4]

def code_label(code: str) -> str:
    dotted = code[:2] + "." + code[2:]
    return SOUSCLASSE_LABEL.get(dotted, code)

LEVELS = [
    ("Section",   code_section),
    ("Division",  code_division),
    ("Group",     code_groupe),
    ("Class",     code_classe),
    ("Sub-class", lambda c: c),
]
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Hierarchical Errors

```{python}
#| label: fig-hierarchy-errors-naf
#| fig-cap: "Among wrong predictions, the coarsest NAF level at which they still land correctly"

ERROR_BUCKETS = ["Class", "Group", "Division", "Section", "No match"]
BUCKET_COLORS = {
    "Class":      "#66BB6A",
    "Group":      "#FFCA28",
    "Division":   "#FB8C00",
    "Section":    "#E53935",
    "No match":   "#7B0000",
}

def _finest_match(true_code: str, pred_code: str) -> str:
    for name, fn in reversed(LEVELS):
        if fn(true_code) == fn(pred_code):
            return name
    return "No match"

error_shares = {}
overall_acc = {}
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL:
    d = preds_by_arch[arch]
    true_codes = [class_code(c) for c in d["y_test"]]
    pred_codes = [class_code(c) for c in d["y_pred"]]
    buckets = [_finest_match(t, p) for t, p in zip(true_codes, pred_codes)]
    overall_acc[arch] = (pd.Series(buckets) == "Sub-class").mean() * 100
    errors = [b for b in buckets if b != "Sub-class"]
    counts = pd.Series(errors).value_counts()
    error_shares[arch] = {b: counts.get(b, 0) / len(errors) * 100 for b in ERROR_BUCKETS}

x_labels = [
    f"{arch}<br><i>({100 - overall_acc[arch]:.1f}% of test set is wrong)</i>"
    for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL
]

fig = go.Figure()
for bucket in ERROR_BUCKETS:
    vals = [error_shares[arch][bucket] for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL]
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
        x=x_labels, y=vals, name=bucket,
        marker=dict(color=BUCKET_COLORS[bucket]),
        text=[f"{v:.1f}%" for v in vals],
        textposition="inside", insidetextfont=dict(color="white", size=11),
        hovertemplate="%{x}<br>" + bucket + ": %{y:.1f}% of errors<extra></extra>",
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    template="simple_white", barmode="stack",
    xaxis_title=None, yaxis_title="Share of wrong predictions (%)",
    yaxis=dict(range=[0, 100]),
    legend_title="Coarsest level where<br>the miss still lands right", height=460,
)
fig.show()
```

Only ≈7–8% of errors stay within the right class — the largest bucket by far, **≈47–48%**, is "No match": missing even the section.

```{python}
for _, r in sample.iterrows():

    examples.append({
        "text": str(r["text"]),
        "true": {name: fmt_level(fn, true_code) for name, fn in LEVELS},
        "preds": {
            arch: {name: fmt_level(fn, class_code(int(r[arch]))) for name, fn in LEVELS}
            for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL
        },
    })

n_grid_cols = 2 + len(ARCHS_AVAIL)

html = f"""
<style>
  .ex-wrap   {{ font-family:sans-serif; font-size:14px; max-width:100%; }}

(function() {{
  const EX = {json.dumps(examples)};

    let head = '<div class="ex-cell ex-hcell">Level</div><div class="ex-cell ex-hcell">True</div>';

      }}
    }}
    document.getElementById('ex-naf-rows').innerHTML = rows;
    document.getElementById('ex-naf-count').textContent = (i + 1) + ' / ' + EX.length;
  }}

  window.exNafNav = function(d) {{ cur = (cur + d + EX.length) % EX.length; render(cur); }};
  render(0);
}})();
</script>
```

## NAF: Explainability — Faithfulness {.smaller}

Progressively delete the most-attributed words and track how fast the model's own confidence collapses, against a random-deletion control.

```{python}
#| label: load-explain-artifacts-naf

EXPLAIN_BUCKET_NAF  = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/explanations/naf"
_ARTIFACT_NAMES_NAF = ["captum.npz", "label_attn.npz", "class_vectors.npz", "faithfulness.npz"]
_NOT_APPLICABLE_NAF = {("pooling", "label_attn.npz")}

def _load_artifact_naf(method: str, name: str):
    if (method, name) in _NOT_APPLICABLE_NAF:
        return None
    cache_dir = Path("results/naf/explain") / method
    cache_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cache = cache_dir / name
    try:
        if not cache.exists():
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{EXPLAIN_BUCKET_NAF}/{method}/{name}", cache)
        return np.load(cache, allow_pickle=True)
    except Exception:
        return None

cap_la, lat_la, cv_la, fai_la = (_load_artifact_naf("labatt",  n) for n in _ARTIFACT_NAMES_NAF)
cap_pl, lat_pl, cv_pl, fai_pl = (_load_artifact_naf("pooling", n) for n in _ARTIFACT_NAMES_NAF)
fai_la_lw = _load_artifact_naf("labatt", "faithfulness_labatt_weight.npz")

HAS_LA   = cap_la is not None
HAS_PL   = cap_pl is not None
HAS_BOTH = HAS_LA and HAS_PL

MODEL_LABELS = {"labatt": "FastText + Label Attention", "pooling": "FastText"}
CAPTUM      = {"labatt": cap_la, "pooling": cap_pl}
FAITHFUL    = {"labatt": fai_la, "pooling": fai_pl}
FAITHFUL_LW = fai_la_lw
MODEL_KEYS  = [k for k in ("labatt", "pooling") if CAPTUM[k] is not None]
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-explain-faithfulness-naf
#| fig-cap: "Faithfulness test: retained probability as top-attributed words are deleted (solid = guided, dotted = random control)."

HAS_FAI_NAF = HAS_LA and all(FAITHFUL.get(k) is not None for k in MODEL_KEYS)

if not HAS_FAI_NAF:
    print("Faithfulness artifacts not yet available.")
else:
    fig_fai_naf = go.Figure()
    for key in MODEL_KEYS:
        fai   = FAITHFUL[key]
        fr    = fai["fractions"]
        color = "#1565C0" if key == "labatt" else "#B71C1C"
        rgb   = "21,101,192" if key == "labatt" else "183,28,28"
        series = [(fai["guided_probs"], "guided by Captum score", "solid", color)]
        if key == "labatt" and FAITHFUL_LW is not None:
            series.append((FAITHFUL_LW["guided_probs"], "guided by attention weights", "solid", "#64B5F6"))
        series.append((fai["random_probs"], "random removal (control)", "dot", color))
        for arr, name, dash, line_color in series:
            m, s = np.nanmean(arr, axis=0), np.nanstd(arr, axis=0)
            fig_fai_naf.add_trace(go.Scatter(
                x=np.concatenate([fr, fr[::-1]]), y=np.concatenate([m + s, (m - s)[::-1]]),
                fill="toself", fillcolor=f"rgba({rgb},0.10)", line=dict(width=0),
                mode="lines", showlegend=False, hoverinfo="skip",
            ))
            fig_fai_naf.add_trace(go.Scatter(
                x=fr, y=m, mode="lines+markers", name=f"{MODEL_LABELS[key]} — {name}",
                line=dict(color=line_color, dash=dash, width=2.5), marker=dict(size=6, color=line_color),
            ))
    fig_fai_naf.update_layout(
        xaxis_title="Fraction of words removed",
        yaxis_title="Mean retained probability of the predicted class",
        yaxis_range=[0, 1.02], paper_bgcolor="white", plot_bgcolor="white",
        height=440, margin=dict(t=20, b=20, l=10, r=10),
        legend=dict(x=1.02, y=1, xanchor="left"),
    )
    fig_fai_naf.show()
```

Label attention's own weights are the **most faithful** guide of the three — a free, more trustworthy explanation at this scale.

## NAF: The Real Problem {.center}

> With a single predicted class, an error is an error.

One model, one flat **679-way** sub-class prediction — no notion of section, division, group or class along the way. As just seen: a wrong prediction is roughly as likely to be **completely off** as it is to be a near-miss, and it's **structural** — not fixed by picking a better architecture.

<div class="cmp2">
<div class="cmp2-col">
<div class="cmp2-title">Today — Wrong Is Wrong</div>
<ul>
<li>One flat sub-class prediction</li>
<li>No notion of "how close"</li>
<li>A miss is a miss, however far off</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="cmp2-col accent">
<div class="cmp2-title">The Goal — Smart Mistakes</div>
<ul>
<li>Hierarchy-aware predictions</li>
<li>Wrong sub-class ≠ wrong section</li>
<li>Fail gracefully, not catastrophically</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>

::: {.fragment}
**The goal isn't fewer errors — it's smarter ones.**
:::

## Towards Multi-Level Classification {.center}

Single-level NAF hits a ceiling on a 679-way problem. **Can predicting all 5 levels jointly push past it?**

## Multi-Level Classification: Architecture {.center}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Intuition

- Give the model that hierarchy explicitly — one independent head per level, on top of a **shared token encoder**
- `L = L_sec + L_div + L_grp + L_cls + L_sub` — **unweighted** sum, backpropagated jointly through the shared trunk
- The bet: learning on **every level at once**, not just the finest one, might push past the ceiling a lone single-level model hits on a 679-way problem
- Goal: not necessarily fewer errors overall, but **smarter** ones — the sub-class head can misfire while section/division heads still land correctly

### Architecture

Benefits from the auxiliary gradient signal of all coarser levels, which pre-shapes the shared representation before the finest-level head has to distinguish between similar sub-classes.">

The token embeddings (B, L, d) from the shared trunk are aggregated into a sentence-level representation in two possible ways:<br>• <b>Mean Pool</b> → (B, d): masked average over real tokens<br>• <b>Label Attention</b> → (B, C<sub>N</sub>, d): one representation per class via cross-attention<br>Having separate aggregators lets each level focus on different aspects of the token sequence.">
```{=html}
        <div style="font-size:13px;color:#1e88e5;">&#x2211;&divide;n</div>
        <div style="font-size:10px;font-weight:700;color:#0d47a1;">SentenceEmbedder</div>

        <div style="font-size:7.5px;color:#888;margin-top:1px;">(B, d) or (B, C, d)</div>

        data-tip="<b>Level-specific Linear head</b><br>Shape depends on the aggregation mode:<br>• <b>Mean Pool</b>: W ∈ ℝ<sup>679 × d</sup> — maps the single (B, d) sentence vector to 679 logits directly.<br>• <b>Label Attention</b>: W ∈ ℝ<sup>1 × d</sup> — the SentenceEmbedder already outputs one (B, C<sub>N</sub>, d) representation per class; the linear scores each independently, then squeeze(-1) yields (B, 679) logits.<br><br>In both cases the output is (B, 679). ### Results
```

```{python}
#| label: load-predictions-naf-multilevel

PRED_BUCKET_ML = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/predictions/naf_multilevel"
ARCH_FILES_ML  = {
    "FastText":                   "fasttext.npz",
    "FastText + Label Attention": "fasttext_labatt.npz",
}
LEVEL_NAMES     = ["sec", "div", "grp", "cls", "sub"]
LEVEL_LABELS_ML = {"sec": "Section", "div": "Division", "grp": "Group", "cls": "Class", "sub": "Sub-class"}

PREDS_DIR_ML = Path("results/naf_multilevel/preds")
PREDS_DIR_ML.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

preds_by_arch_ml = {}
for arch, fname in ARCH_FILES_ML.items():
    cache = PREDS_DIR_ML / fname
    try:
        if not cache.exists():
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(f"{PRED_BUCKET_ML}/{fname}", cache)
        d = np.load(cache, allow_pickle=True)
        preds_by_arch_ml[arch] = {"y_test": d["y_test"].astype(int)}
        preds_by_arch_ml[arch].update({
            f"y_pred_{lvl}": d[f"y_pred_{lvl}"].astype(int) for lvl in LEVEL_NAMES
        })
    except Exception:
        pass

ARCHS_AVAIL_ML = list(preds_by_arch_ml.keys())

NAF_PARQUET_URL = "https://minio.lab.sspcloud.fr/projet-text-classif/datasets/naf_merged.parquet"

classes_cache = PREDS_DIR_ML / "level_classes.json"
if classes_cache.exists():
    LEVEL_CLASSES = json.loads(classes_cache.read_text())
else:
    df_full_ml = pd.read_parquet(NAF_PARQUET_URL, columns=["libelle_cleaned"] + LEVEL_NAMES).dropna()
    LEVEL_CLASSES = {lvl: sorted(df_full_ml[lvl].astype(str).unique().tolist()) for lvl in LEVEL_NAMES}
    classes_cache.write_text(json.dumps(LEVEL_CLASSES))

test_cache = PREDS_DIR_ML / "test_reconstruction.parquet"
if test_cache.exists():
    df_test_ml = pd.read_parquet(test_cache)
else:
    df_full_ml = pd.read_parquet(NAF_PARQUET_URL, columns=["libelle_cleaned"] + LEVEL_NAMES)
    df_full_ml = df_full_ml.dropna().reset_index(drop=True)
    df_full_ml = df_full_ml.sample(frac=1, random_state=42).reset_index(drop=True)
    df_test_ml = df_full_ml.iloc[len(df_full_ml) - 50000:].reset_index(drop=True)
    df_test_ml.to_parquet(test_cache)

X_TEST_ML = df_test_ml["libelle_cleaned"].values

with open("assets/naf2025_structure.json") as f:
    _naf_struct_ml = json.load(f)
SECTION_LABEL_ML     = {s["id"]: s["label"] for s in _naf_struct_ml["sections"]}
SOUSCLASSE_LABEL_ML  = _naf_struct_ml["sousclasses"]

def code_of(level: str, idx: int) -> str:
    return LEVEL_CLASSES[level][idx]

def label_of(level: str, code: str) -> str:
    if level == "sec":
        return SECTION_LABEL_ML.get(code, code)
    if level == "div":
        return _naf_struct_ml["divisions"].get(code, {}).get("label", code)
    if level == "sub":
        dotted = code[:2] + "." + code[2:]
        return SOUSCLASSE_LABEL_ML.get(dotted, code)
    return code

# Single-level's raw sub-class-only predictions, so its truncation-derived
# cascade can be plotted on the same axes for comparison.
DIVISION_TO_SECTION_SINGLE = DIVISION_TO_SECTION

SINGLE_LEVELS = [
    ("Section",   lambda c: DIVISION_TO_SECTION_SINGLE.get(c[:2], "?")),
    ("Division",  lambda c: c[:2]),
    ("Group",     lambda c: c[:3]),
    ("Class",     lambda c: c[:4]),
    ("Sub-class", lambda c: c),
]

def _single_class_code(idx):
    return class_code(idx)

preds_by_arch_single = preds_by_arch
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-hierarchy-errors-naf-multilevel
#| fig-cap: "Among wrong sub-class predictions, the finest level that still lands correctly — multi-level's independent heads vs. single-level's truncated cascade"

BUCKET_ORDER_ML  = ["cls", "grp", "div", "sec"]
BUCKET_LABELS_ML = {"cls": "Class", "grp": "Group", "div": "Division", "sec": "Section"}
ERROR_BUCKETS_ML = ["Class", "Group", "Division", "Section", "No match"]
BUCKET_COLORS_ML = {
    "Class":      "#66BB6A",
    "Group":      "#FFCA28",
    "Division":   "#FB8C00",
    "Section":    "#E53935",
    "No match":   "#7B0000",
}

error_shares_ml = {}
overall_acc_ml  = {}
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL_ML:
    d = preds_by_arch_ml[arch]
    y_test  = d["y_test"]
    correct = {lvl: (d[f"y_pred_{lvl}"] == y_test[:, i]) for i, lvl in enumerate(LEVEL_NAMES)}
    overall_acc_ml[arch] = correct["sub"].mean() * 100

    wrong_idx = np.where(~correct["sub"])[0]
    assigned  = np.full(len(wrong_idx), "No match", dtype=object)
    remaining = np.ones(len(wrong_idx), dtype=bool)
    for lvl in BUCKET_ORDER_ML:
        is_correct_here = correct[lvl][wrong_idx] & remaining
        assigned[is_correct_here] = BUCKET_LABELS_ML[lvl]
        remaining &= ~is_correct_here

    counts = pd.Series(assigned).value_counts()
    error_shares_ml[arch] = {b: counts.get(b, 0) / len(wrong_idx) * 100 for b in ERROR_BUCKETS_ML}

SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY = {name: fn for name, fn in SINGLE_LEVELS}
SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY = {
    "sec": SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY["Section"],
    "div": SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY["Division"],
    "grp": SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY["Group"],
    "cls": SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY["Class"],
}

error_shares_single = {}
overall_acc_single  = {}
for arch, d in preds_by_arch_single.items():
    true_codes  = np.array([_single_class_code(c) for c in d["y_test"]])
    pred_codes  = np.array([_single_class_code(c) for c in d["y_pred"]])
    correct_sub = true_codes == pred_codes
    overall_acc_single[arch] = correct_sub.mean() * 100

    wrong_idx = np.where(~correct_sub)[0]
    t_wrong, p_wrong = true_codes[wrong_idx], pred_codes[wrong_idx]
    assigned  = np.full(len(wrong_idx), "No match", dtype=object)
    remaining = np.ones(len(wrong_idx), dtype=bool)
    for lvl in BUCKET_ORDER_ML:
        fn = SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY[lvl]
        is_correct_here = (np.array([fn(t) for t in t_wrong]) == np.array([fn(p) for p in p_wrong])) & remaining
        assigned[is_correct_here] = BUCKET_LABELS_ML[lvl]
        remaining &= ~is_correct_here

    counts = pd.Series(assigned).value_counts()
    error_shares_single[arch] = {b: counts.get(b, 0) / len(wrong_idx) * 100 for b in ERROR_BUCKETS_ML}

bar_order = []
for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL_ML:
    bar_order.append(("ml", arch))
    if arch in preds_by_arch_single:
        bar_order.append(("single", arch))

x_labels_combined = [
    f"{arch}<br>multi-level<i> ({100 - overall_acc_ml[arch]:.1f}% wrong)</i>" if kind == "ml"
    else f"{arch}<br>single-level<i> ({100 - overall_acc_single[arch]:.1f}% wrong)</i>"
    for kind, arch in bar_order
]
patterns_combined = ["" if kind == "ml" else "/" for kind, arch in bar_order]

fig = go.Figure()
for bucket in ERROR_BUCKETS_ML:
    vals = [
        error_shares_ml[arch][bucket] if kind == "ml" else error_shares_single[arch][bucket]
        for kind, arch in bar_order
    ]
    fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
        x=x_labels_combined, y=vals, name=bucket,
        marker=dict(color=BUCKET_COLORS_ML[bucket], pattern=dict(shape=patterns_combined)),
        text=[f"{v:.1f}%" for v in vals],
        textposition="inside", insidetextfont=dict(color="white", size=11),
        hovertemplate="%{x}<br>" + bucket + ": %{y:.1f}% of errors<extra></extra>",
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    template="simple_white", barmode="stack",
    xaxis_title=None, yaxis_title="Share of wrong sub-class predictions (%)",
    yaxis=dict(range=[0, 100]),
    legend_title="Finest level<br>that still lands right", height=440,
)
fig.show()
```

We reason directly with each head's own prediction, independently — not by truncating the sub-class guess.

### Examples

```{python}
#| label: fig-examples-naf-multilevel
#| fig-cap: "Example predictions across all five hierarchy levels"

import random
random.seed(42)

y_test_all_ml = preds_by_arch_ml[ARCHS_AVAIL_ML[0]]["y_test"]  # (50000, 5)

df_ex_ml = pd.DataFrame({"text": X_TEST_ML})
for i, lvl in enumerate(LEVEL_NAMES):
    df_ex_ml[f"true_{lvl}"] = y_test_all_ml[:, i]
    for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL_ML:
        df_ex_ml[f"{arch}__{lvl}"] = preds_by_arch_ml[arch][f"y_pred_{lvl}"]

sub_cols_ml = [f"{arch}__sub" for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL_ML]
df_ex_ml["disagree"]  = df_ex_ml[sub_cols_ml].nunique(axis=1) > 1
df_ex_ml["any_wrong"] = (df_ex_ml[sub_cols_ml].values != df_ex_ml[["true_sub"]].values).any(axis=1)
pool_ml   = df_ex_ml[df_ex_ml["disagree"] & df_ex_ml["any_wrong"]]
sample_ml = pool_ml.sample(min(12, len(pool_ml)), random_state=42).reset_index(drop=True)

def fmt_ml(level, idx):
    code = code_of(level, int(idx))
    lbl  = label_of(level, code)
    return f"{code} — {lbl}" if lbl != code else code

def fmt_code_ml(level, code):
    lbl = label_of(level, code)
    return f"{code} — {lbl}" if lbl != code else code

def truncate_code_ml(level, code):
    return code if level == "sub" else SINGLE_LEVEL_FN_BY_KEY[level](code)

# Text -> row lookup into the single-level page's own (separately trained)
# test set, so each sampled utterance can be matched to its single-level
# prediction too.
single_lookup_ml = {
    arch: {str(t): i for i, t in enumerate(d["X_test"])}
    for arch, d in preds_by_arch_single.items()
}

examples_ml = []
for _, r in sample_ml.iterrows():
    text = str(r["text"])
    preds_entry = {}
    for arch in ARCHS_AVAIL_ML:
        sub_code_own = code_of("sub", int(r[f"{arch}__sub"]))
        preds_entry[arch] = {
            "direct":     {lvl: fmt_ml(lvl, r[f"{arch}__{lvl}"]) for lvl in LEVEL_NAMES},
            "trunc_own":  {lvl: fmt_code_ml(lvl, truncate_code_ml(lvl, sub_code_own)) for lvl in LEVEL_NAMES},
            "trunc_single": None,
        }
        idx_single = single_lookup_ml.get(arch, {}).get(text)
        if idx_single is not None:
            sub_code_single = _single_class_code(int(preds_by_arch_single[arch]["y_pred"][idx_single]))
            preds_entry[arch]["trunc_single"] = {
                lvl: fmt_code_ml(lvl, truncate_code_ml(lvl, sub_code_single)) for lvl in LEVEL_NAMES
            }

    examples_ml.append({
        "text": text,
        "true": {lvl: fmt_ml(lvl, r[f"true_{lvl}"]) for lvl in LEVEL_NAMES},
        "preds": preds_entry,
    })

</style>

<div class="exml-wrap">

    <button class="exml-btn" onclick="exNafMlNav(-1)">← Prev</button>
    <span class="exml-count" id="exml-count"></span>
    <button class="exml-btn" onclick="exNafMlNav(1)">Next →</button>
  </div>

    <div class="exml-text" id="exml-text"></div>
    <div id="exml-table-wrap"></div>
  </div>
</div>

<script>
(function() {{
  const EX = {json.dumps(examples_ml)};
  const LEVELS = {json.dumps(LEVEL_NAMES)};
  const LEVEL_LABELS = {json.dumps(LEVEL_LABELS_ML)};
  const ARCHS = {json.dumps(ARCHS_AVAIL_ML)};
  const ARCH_SHORT = {json.dumps({"FastText": "FT", "FastText + Label Attention": "FT+LabAtt"})};
  let cur = 0;

  function render(i) {{
    const e = EX[i];
    document.getElementById('exml-text').textContent = '"' + e.text + '"';

    let head = '<th>Prediction</th>';
    for (const lvl of LEVELS) head += '<th>' + LEVEL_LABELS[lvl] + '</th>';
    head = '<tr>' + head + '</tr>';

    let rows = '<tr><td class="exml-lvl">True</td>';
    for (const lvl of LEVELS) rows += '<td>' + e.true[lvl] + '</td>';
    rows += '</tr>';

    for (const arch of ARCHS) {{
      const p = e.preds[arch];
      const archShort = ARCH_SHORT[arch] || arch;
      const variantDefs = [['Indep. heads', p.direct], ['Trunc. (multi)', p.trunc_own], ['Trunc. (single)', p.trunc_single]];
      for (const [label, data] of variantDefs) {{
        rows += '<tr><td class="exml-lvl">' + archShort + ' — ' + label + '</td>';
        for (const lvl of LEVELS) {{
          if (!data) {{
            rows += '<td style="color:#aaa;">n/a</td>';
          }} else {{
            const val = data[lvl];
            const cls = val === e.true[lvl] ? 'exml-correct' : 'exml-wrong';
            rows += '<td><span class="' + cls + '">' + val + '</span></td>';
          }}
        }}
        rows += '</tr>';
      }}
    }}
    document.getElementById('exml-table-wrap').innerHTML =
      '<table class="exml-table"><thead>' + head + '</thead><tbody>' + rows + '</tbody></table>';
    document.getElementById('exml-count').textContent = (i + 1) + ' / ' + EX.length;
  }}

  window.exNafMlNav = function(d) {{ cur = (cur + d + EX.length) % EX.length; render(cur); }};
  render(0);
}})();
</script>
"""
HTML(html)
```

<p style="font-size:1.15em;">The heads are <strong>independent</strong>: a fine level can land right while a coarser one misses — <strong>impossible before</strong>.</p>

:::

## Multi-Level: A New Problem Appears {.center}

- The 5 heads are trained jointly but **never compared to each other** at inference — nothing in the loss enforces agreement
- Consequence: heads can produce **mutually inconsistent codes** — e.g. the section head says "C" while the true parent of the predicted sub-class is section "A"

::: {.fragment}
> As is, that's not useful for a human annotator — but a smarter, consistency-aware model could at least hand them better guidance.
:::

## Multi-Level: Going Further {.center}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Consistency Loss

<p style="font-size:0.65em;"><strong>Intuition</strong>: add a sixth loss term that directly penalizes disagreement between <em>adjacent</em> levels.</p>

```{=html}
<div class="gf1-link">

<small style="color:#c62828;">&#10007; parent-of(&ldquo;62&rdquo;) = J</small>
</div>
<div class="gf1-blk">
<div class="gf1-lbl" style="color:#1976D2;">Division</div>
<div class="gf1-chip" style="background:#e0e9f7;border:1.5px solid #1976D2;">
<div class="gf1-code" style="color:#0d47a1;">&quot;62&quot;</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="gf1-link">
<span style="color:#2e7d32;">&#8596;</span>
<small style="color:#2e7d32;">&#10003; agree</small>
</div>
<div class="gf1-blk">
<div class="gf1-lbl" style="color:#1e88e5;">Group</div>
<div class="gf1-chip" style="background:#d8e6f6;border:1.5px solid #1e88e5;">
<div class="gf1-code" style="color:#0d47a1;">&quot;620&quot;</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="gf1-link">
<span style="color:#2e7d32;">&#8596;</span>
<small style="color:#2e7d32;">&#10003; agree</small>
</div>
<div class="gf1-blk">
<div class="gf1-lbl" style="color:#2196F3;">Class</div>
<div class="gf1-chip" style="background:#cfe0fb;border:1.5px solid #2196F3;">
<div class="gf1-code" style="color:#0d47a1;">&quot;6201&quot;</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="gf1-link">
<span style="color:#2e7d32;">&#8596;</span>
<small style="color:#2e7d32;">&#10003; agree</small>
</div>
<div class="gf1-blk">
<div class="gf1-lbl" style="color:#42A5F5;">Sub-class</div>
<div class="gf1-chip" style="background:#c5dafa;border:1.5px solid #42A5F5;">
<div class="gf1-code" style="color:#0d47a1;">&quot;6201Y&quot;</div>
</div>
</div>
</div>


<div style="display:flex;justify-content:center;gap:14px;margin-top:10px;flex-wrap:wrap;">
<div style="background:#e0f2f1;border:1.5px dashed #00897b;border-radius:9px;padding:10px 18px;text-align:center;max-width:400px;">
<div style="font-size:8.5px;font-weight:700;color:#00695c;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.06em;margin-bottom:4px;">New term &mdash; sum over adjacent pairs only</div>
<div style="font-size:13px;font-weight:700;color:#00695c;">
ℒ<sub>cons</sub> = &sum;<sub>k</sub> CE( P(L<sub>k</sub>),
parent-of(argmax&nbsp;P(L<sub>k+1</sub>)) )
</div>
<div style="font-size:8px;color:#00897b;margin-top:4px;">
L<sub>1..5</sub> = Section, Division, Group, Class, Sub-class
</div>
</div>

<div style="background:#fce4ec;border:1.5px solid #e91e63;border-radius:9px;padding:10px 20px;text-align:center;display:flex;align-items:center;">
<div style="font-size:12.5px;font-weight:700;color:#c2185b;">
ℒ = ℒ<sub>sec</sub>+ℒ<sub>div</sub>+ℒ<sub>grp</sub>+ℒ<sub>cls</sub>+ℒ<sub>sub</sub> &nbsp;+&nbsp; λ&middot;ℒ<sub>cons</sub>
</div>
</div>
</div>

</div>
</div>
```

<div class="cmp2" style="font-size:0.82em;">
<div class="cmp2-col accent">
<div class="cmp2-title">Pros</div>
<ul>
<li>Minimal change — only the loss changes</li>
<li>Targets the exact failure mode measured</li>
<li>One scalar λ tunes the trade-off, can be annealed over training</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="cmp2-col">
<div class="cmp2-title">Cons</div>
<ul>
<li>Only a <em>soft</em> constraint — disagreement less likely, never impossible</li>
<li>The clean differentiable version needs a full class→parent membership matrix per adjacent pair</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>

```{=html}
<div class="cmp2 cmp2-tight">
<div class="cmp2-col accent">
<div class="cmp2-title">Pros</div>
<ul>
<li>Consistency <strong>by construction</strong> — a finer head structurally cannot ignore the coarser levels</li>
<li>Mirrors the coding-officer workflow: section first, then narrow down</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="cmp2-col">
<div class="cmp2-title">Cons</div>
<ul>
<li>Purely sequential — 5 heads deep, slower to train and to run than parallel heads</li>
<li>Errors <strong>propagate forward</strong> — a wrong section can drag every downstream head down with it</li>
</ul>
```

```{=html}
  </div>
  <p style="text-align:center;font-size:8px;color:#999;margin-top:8px;">Same e<sub>fused</sub> feeds all five heads — only their own weights (W<sub>sec</sub>&hellip;W<sub>sub</sub>) can still make them disagree.</p>

</div>
</div>

<div class="cmp2 cmp2-tight" style="margin-top:14px;">
<div class="cmp2-col accent">
<div class="cmp2-title">Pros</div>
<ul>
<li>Removes one whole source of disagreement for free: identical input to every head</li>
<li>Still one parallel pass — much closer to today's cost than the cascade</li>
<li>No extra module to train — the mean is parameter-free</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="cmp2-col">
<div class="cmp2-title">Cons</div>
<ul>
<li>Trades away per-level specialisation: fine-grained signal gets diluted into the average</li>
<li>Every head reasons from the same coarse summary, not from what makes its own level distinctive</li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>

</div>
```

:::

# Technical Conclusion

## Answering the Internship's Objectives {.center}

::: {.fragment}
**1. Accuracy vs. cost** — Lightweight architectures are competitive, and label attention's extra expressiveness is real — but it only pays off once there is enough data *per class*. Confirmed twice: CLINC150 vs. Amazon, then again on NAF at 1.2M-example scale.
:::

::: {.fragment}
**2. Trustworthy explanations** — Through extensive testing and illustration, we succeeded in identifying **what drove the model to give a given answer**.
:::

::: {.fragment}
**3. Hierarchy** — Dedicated per-level heads cut the "completely wrong" rate from ~47% to 29–34%, and clearly beat truncating a flat prediction — but introduce a **head-disagreement problem** that this internship identifies without yet solving.
:::

# Personal Assessment

## Skills Developed {.center}

- **End-to-end ML engineering at production scale**: PyTorch Lightning, Hydra-based configuration, MLflow experiment tracking, GPU sweeps orchestrated with Kubernetes / Argo Workflows
- **Explainability in practice**: Captum Integrated Gradients, attention-based interpretability, and how to actually *measure* whether an explanation is faithful rather than just plausible-looking
- **Scientific communication**: structuring three months of experiments into a public, reproducible Quarto report and a reusable, config-driven codebase
- **Working with a real, production dataset**: this is not a clean academic benchmark — it actually feeds a production system at INSEE, which changes everything about how the work has to be done
- **Team communication & collaboration**: discussing and iterating with the team, and especially collaborating on GitHub — branches, pull requests, code review — where I learned a lot about the field's best practices
